title: Breaking More Encrypted USB Drives with AI
content_md: Earlier this year, I showed how to break encrypted USB drives with time-travel debugging ( slides ) at RE//verse . After having a lot of recent success with AI-assisted reverse engineering and vulnerability research, I wanted to see how well AI could handle the same tasks. Not surprisingly, it exceeded my expectations. In one case, it reproduced my research in seven minutes using static analysis. I then asked it to analyze two products I had not considered in my original research, and it tore those apart just as easily. Breaking NetacFileLock again I started with NetacFileLock , which I had previously analyzed using time-travel debugging (TTD) to trace the ciphertext back to its AES key. I only did one prompt: This is a file encryption utility. Analyze its crypto system and see if it is secure. You can use Binary Ninja MCP to help you. Within seven minutes, Codex reached the main flaw: the program initialized AES-256 with a fixed 32-byte key embedded in the executable. The user password was checked separately and did not determine the encryption key. This means anyone can decrypt the file without knowing the user password.
